title: Asking for a sheet of components gives a clean, titled table of them in their states
goal: When a person asks for a set of components shown in their states, Ask and the Photonz skill lay them out as a tidy table: a title, a header for each state, one row per component, every cell lined up, one type scale throughout, and the components' own words changed rather than new words laid over them. It should look like a page from Apple's design kit.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-20 07:38 (screenshot queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-component-sheet-mess.png): 'this is a complete mess. there is no table, no alignment, no titles, no clean design.' The run placed five components at their default spots and laid five add_text calls over them at body size.

Likely ways in, decide and log: a layout tool the model can call (a grid or table: rows, columns, gap, the layout engine set_layout already uses) so the model names cells instead of coordinates; a component sheet as a built-in recipe; the skill's instructions saying how a sheet is built; giving the model the components' variants and text fields up front. Climb with the eval: keep a change only if the score goes up.
acceptance: The request 'create a table of apple like quality base components that show different states and text' on a blank picture gives: a sheet title, column headers for the states (for example Default, Hover, Pressed, Disabled), a row label per component, each component in each state placed in its cell, cells on one grid with equal gaps, and no text over another layer
States are real: each cell is the component in that state (its own variant or look), not the same component copied with a label
Type follows one scale: at most four sizes on the sheet, headers and labels share one style each

Scored with the eval (a-scored-test-set-for-what-ask-and-the-photonz-s): the component sheet cases reach at least 8 of 10 on every rubric line, for Ask on this Mac and for the skill, and the before and after scores are in the audit

Audit under queue/audits/ with the before (queue/audits/2026-10-20-user-ask-component-sheet-mess.png) and after pictures. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: intake: waits on the eval task so the climb is measured

eval landed: cases component-table (the user's words) and design-system-sheet. Baselines 2026-10-20: Ask 39.2 and 55.6 (judge 2.4 and 3.6 of 10); skill 75.2 and 72 (judge 7.6 and 6). The skill's table leaves most of the canvas empty and its hover looks like default. Rules read the document: title, state headers, labelled rows, alignment, type sizes, words over controls. Run: Scripts/ask-eval.sh run --engine ask|skill --cases component-table,design-system-sheet --tag '<change>'.

From asking-for-base-components-builds-the-real-set-w (2026-10-23): add_component now makes a component with its states as versions in one call, and labels:true names its row on the left and each state above its look; Ask lines labelled rows up on one x and one column step (AskConversation.alignSheet) and stops a sheet when the canvas is full. What is still yours: one header row instead of a caption over every look, a true grid, equal row gaps. Ask component-table is 47.7 now, skill 84.4.

Built: every labelled add_component lays every labelled row on the canvas out as one table (Sources/PhotonzCore/AgentComponentSheet.swift): header row naming each state once over its column, names on one left edge, looks centred in cells on one grid filling the width with even margins, rows 32 apart. Rows found by their copies too, since the editor parks originals in the Library (the first eval run piled every row on one y for exactly that). Chose a header row per group of rows sharing their states (sheetSections) over one header with odd states under someone else's column, because the judge read a toggle's On under Hover as wrong. App grows the canvas from the laid-out table in the same undo step (AgentDesignWork.addComponent); the planner's estimated canvas_size steps are gone. add_component now refuses words on top of words and words longer than their box, estimated from font size so Ask's planner refuses before building. Skill recipe and agent-mcp.md updated.

Eval (rubric f5ae1562). Skill component-table 88.8 (was 84.4): clean 8, typography 8, aligned 8, designed 8, didWhatWasAsked 9, every line at the bar. Skill design-system-sheet 86.4 (baseline 61.7): 8, 8, aligned 7, 8, 8. Ask component-table 52 (was 49.4; rules 9.8, noOverlap 10): judge 6, 6, 6, 5, 5. Ask design-system-sheet 52.8 (was 59.2; a blind look is worth several points, read with care): 3, 5, 4, 4, 6. NOT at the bar: Ask is 3 to 6 per line and the skill's design sheet has aligned 7. What holds Ask back is inside its own drawings (a checkbox labelled Off drawn checked, toggle and switch both drawn, states that barely differ, card text past the card) and the model's row order, not the table. Left pending for that.

Tried and reverted: a two line prompt edit (each kind once, same state names across kinds) was followed by two design-system-sheet runs timing out in planning at 300 s; with it reverted the case ran in 91 s. Not proven to be the cause (the second also overlapped the full test suite), so not kept.

Follow-up filed: the-name-chips-over-component-copies-stay-clear (p1). The window capture shows the canvas name chip over each copy covering the header row at normal zoom; the export is clean. Left rough here: rows with fewer states leave empty cells the judge calls holes; grouping rows by states can reorder the model's rows.

Audit: queue/audits/2026-10-23-component-sheet-table.json (before 2026-10-20-user-ask-component-sheet-mess.png, after pictures for Ask and skill, window capture). Pictures looked at: Ask after shows a titled table, each group headed, no words overlapping, flaws in the drawings themselves; skill after reads as a design-kit page; window capture shows chips over headers. Tests: Scripts/test.sh 14289 passed; ask-builds-base-components-walk passes.

Table layout shipped (dafd16e6) and the skill's request clears 8 on every line, but Ask on this Mac is at 5 to 6 and the skill's design sheet has aligned 7: the 8 of 10 bar is not met, so it stays open.
